paper.title: Multiarmed Bandits With Limited Expert Advice

settings.name_in_paper: advice-efficient multiarmed bandits with expert advice (limited advice)
unmapped: Learner may observe the advice of at most M_adv of the N experts in each round (limited advice)
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t = 1, 2, \ldots, T$, we are required to pull one arm $A_t \in \{1, 2, \ldots, K\} =: \mK$. Simultaneously, an adversary sets losses $\ell_t(a) \in [0, 1]$ for each arm $a \in \mK$. Assisting us in this task are $N$ experts ... The catch is that we can only observe the advice of at most $M$ experts of our choosing in each round.

symbols.M_adv: number of experts whose advice can be queried per round

tuning: eta = sqrt(M log(N)/(K' N T)) (proof uses sqrt(2 M log N/(K' N T)))

source.label: thm:mw
source.quote: Set $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{M \log(N)}{K'NT}}$. Then the expected regret of the algorithm using the \MW forecaster is bounded by $\sqrt{\frac{2K'N \log(N)}{M} T}$.

results.notes: K' = min{K,M}. Statement's eta differs from the proof's by a factor sqrt(2).

symbols.M_adv: number of experts whose advice can be queried per round

source.label: thm:inf
source.quote: Set  $c = \log(\tfrac{8M}{K'})$ and $\eta = 2N^{\frac{1}{2c}}[c(RK')^{1 - \cinv}T]^{-\frac{1}{2}}$. Then the expected regret of the algorithm using the \INF forecaster is bounded by $4\sqrt{\frac{K'N\log(\tfrac{8M}{K'})}{M} T}$.

symbols.M_adv: number of experts whose advice can be queried per round

conditions: hard instance: random uniform advice, Bernoulli losses with best expert's arm having mean 1/2 - eps

source.quote: For any algorithm for the multiarmed bandit with limited expert advice setting, there is a sequence of expert advices and losses for each arm so that the expected regret of the algorithm is at least $\Omega\bigP{\sqrt{\frac{N}{f(K, M)} T}} = \Omega\bigP{\sqrt{\frac{\min\{K, \frac{M}{\log(K)}\} N}{M}T}}$.

results.notes: Also stated as Omega(sqrt(N T / f(K,M))) where f(K,M) is expected max load of M balls into K bins; proof gives (1/32) sqrt(N T/f(K,M)).
